title: Top 8 Forever — Scene Kid Starfield
description: A pixel-faithful recreation of a 2006 MySpace profile layout: starfield void, glitter-bordered photo box, marquee text strip, and a grayscale Top 8 friends grid. Emo-coded, unapologetically so.
philosophy: This template exists because early social media was the last moment mass self-expression was genuinely ugly on purpose — and that ugliness had soul. It refuses clean grids, readable hierarchy, and any instinct toward brand consistency. It is built for speakers who use nostalgia as rhetoric and audiences who remember picking a profile song at 2am. If the room expects professionalism, this is the wrong room.
goodFor: Nostalgia-arc brand retrospectives aimed at millennial audiences
Cultural commentary on early internet identity and self-expression
Portfolio openers for designers with an explicit Y2K or emo aesthetic
Social media history or digital anthropology presentation segments
avoidFor: Corporate quarterly earnings or investor decks
Academic conference presentations requiring perceived credibility
Chart-heavy data reviews where legibility is non-negotiable
Any context where the speaker needs the audience to trust them immediately
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The opening slide should feel like loading a stranger's meticulously curated MySpace profile at 2am — the starfield void stretches infinitely and slightly menacingly, glitter borders pulse with lo-fi digital energy, and the overall composition weaponizes asymmetric clutter as deliberate identity. Hero text collides with decorative frames rather than sitting above them in polite hierarchy. Avoid any implication that whitespace is virtuous; the mood is unapologetically maximal, emo-coded, and structured around self-expression as spectacle rather than clarity.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed starfield void with zero outer margin — background bleeds to all four edges with no gutter. Title anchors asymmetrically to the left two-fifths of the slide, broken across two ragged lines, while a glitter-bordered rectangular photo/hero box bleeds in from the right edge and overlaps the title zone. A marquee-style text strip — scrolling declaration or deck subtitle — runs as a horizontal band across the lower quarter of the slide. No page number; a decorative badge element (star cluster or pixelated glyph) occupies the bottom-right corner as a signature mark.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like stumbling onto a stranger's carefully curated MySpace profile at 2am — claustrophobic with intention, every zone competing for emotional primacy. Mood is dramatic and confessional: a starfield void pressing in from all edges, glitter borders crackling against the dark as structural punctuation rather than ornament. Composition is dense-modular without resolution — panels stack and slightly overlap as if hand-coded in raw inline CSS by someone who meant it. Avoid whitespace comfort, editorial restraint, or any sense of unified visual language; the clutter is the rhetoric.

examples.layoutNotes: Two asymmetric column zones mimic a MySpace profile div stack: a narrow left sidebar (~28% width) and a wider right main panel (~67% width) with a deliberate few-pixel overlap suggesting raw CSS absolute positioning. Core content lives inside a glitter-bordered box occupying the right panel — border treated as a structural element, not decoration. A marquee-style text strip runs full-bleed at the bottom edge, independent of both columns. Decorative star/pixel scatter elements float in the upper corners outside column logic; no baseline grid enforced, vertical rhythm is intentionally broken by competing box heights.
